title: PointwiseHessianStationarity.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained optimization of a C³ function f: ℝᵈ → ℝ. Nonconvex objectives are permitted; f(0)−inf f≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The gradient is exact at every queried point, independently of history and oracle seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each query returns the exact function value together with the gradient and full Hessian.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact full-Hessian oracle: one bundled call returns (f(x),∇f(x),∇²f(x)); there is no oracle error.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Pointwise third-derivative bound ‖D²(∇f)(x)‖≤L₀+L₁‖∇f(x)‖ for every x, using induced operator norms. L₀,L₁≥0 and L₀+L₁>0; no global Hessian-norm bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space ℝᵈ. Writing Q=Δ√(L₀+L₁ε)/ε^(3/2), validity requires Q≥2³⁹ and d≥2¹⁴⁰(1+⌈Q⌉₊)⁴.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters d,L₀,L₁,Δ,G,ε are public. The unknown objective satisfies f(0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x and ‖∇f(0)‖≤G, with Δ,ε>0 and G≥16ε. Algorithms have no additional structural restriction.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianStationarity.lean: Params, broadSpec.Public, broadSpec.publicInput, broadSpec.admissible, spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Setup.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output is a point X satisfying E[‖∇f(X)‖]≤ε, with the norm to the first power. The output must be measurable and its gradient norm integrable.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the algorithm and oracle seed laws. Exact oracle replies leave algorithmic randomization possible; oracle execution uses a fixed call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation uses a gradient-dependent pointwise third-derivative bound and explicit large-dimension parameter restrictions within an exact second-order oracle stationarity problem.

descriptionHtml:
Stationarity with Exact Hessian Access

We seek approximate stationarity of a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d is a nonnegative integer. The function is three times continuously differentiable, with third-derivative norm bounded by L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥ at each point x, where L0,L1≥0 and L0+L1>0. At the reference point x0=0, the objective gap above the infimum is at most Δ>0 and the gradient norm is at most G≥0. The oracle returns the exact value, gradient, and Hessian. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ with EP∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). We use the Euclidean norm on Rd. Derivative norms ∥⋅∥op are the induced operator norms; in particular, ∇2f(x) is a linear operator on Rd, and ∇3f(x) is a trilinear form. The algorithm receives d,L0,L1,Δ,G, and ε.

The parameter regime is restricted by 16ε≤G,ρ:=ΔL0+L1εε3/2≥239,d≥2140(1+⌈ρ⌉)4. Here ⌈ρ⌉ is the least integer greater than or equal to ρ.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Third-derivative bound). The function f belongs to C3(Rd;R) and satisfies ∥∇3f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective and gradient control). At the reference point x0=0, f(x0)−f(x)≤Δfor every x∈Rd,∥∇f(x0)∥≤G.

Queries may be made at any x∈Rd. Each oracle call returns (f(x),∇f(x),∇2f(x)). After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈Rd must be measurable under P, its gradient norm must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
f:Rd→R is C3, with ∥D3f(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥, f(0)−inff≤Δ, and ∥∇f(0)∥≤G. Here L0,L1≥0, L0+L1>0, Δ,ε>0, G≥16ε, S≥239, and d≥2140(1+⌈S⌉)4; S is defined below. Each query returns exact (f,∇f,∇2f); the setup imposes no algorithm restriction. The target is measurable X with integrable gradient norm and ∫∥∇f(X(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε, for the algorithm’s seed law P. The paired bounds match in their polynomial terms; the additive logarithm in (2) is not matched by (1).

Stationarity under pointwise Hessian growth: PointwiseHessianStationarity.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations

(1) PointwiseHessianStationarityLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review)

Lower bound

 Necessary: Ω(S) joint calls. Failure for every randomized adaptive algorithm at every integer budget b≤⌊S/239⌋; instance independent of the realized seed.

(2) PointwiseHessianStationarity (Ours) (review)

Upper bound

Sufficient joint calls:

O(S+log(2+L1GL0+L1ε)).

(3) (Carmon et al. 2020), Theorem 2, p=2

Lower bound; Lipschitz-Hessian subclass

 Necessary: Ω(ΔL0ε−3/2), L0>0. Randomized algorithms, even with all derivatives; d≳1+T2log⁡(2+T). (1): Necessary budget increases by 1+L1ε/L0; polynomial gain when L1ε≫L0. Scope: also covers L0=0. (1): Requires dimension of order S4, rather than T2log⁡(2+T); also needs G≥16ε and S≥239.

(4) Cubic Newton (Fang et al. 2026), Corollary 1

Upper bound; pointwise condition

Sufficient joint calls, including backtracking:

O(S+log(2+L1GL0+L13/2Δ)). Use σinit=L0+L1ε, δ=L0ε+L1ε; for L0=0, substitute L0′=L1ε.

 (2): Matches known polynomial rate, with a different additive logarithm; formalizes the transfer to a joint oracle. (2): Needs L0,L1,Δ,G,ε; larger leading constant. Loses the ∇2f⪰−δI guarantee and parameter-free updates; restricted to the stated G,S,d regime.

Abbr: S=ΔL0+L1εε−3/2≍ΔL0ε−3/2+ΔL1ε−1; T=ΔL0ε−3/2. D3f denotes the third derivative with operator norm; ∇2f is the Hessian; δ is curvature tolerance; σinit is the initial cubic regularization parameter. O and Ω suppress universal constants; ≳ and ≍ are comparisons up to universal constants.

Carmon, Yair, John C. Duchi, Oliver Hinder, and Aaron Sidford. 2020. “Lower Bounds for Finding Stationary Points I.” Mathematical Programming 184: 71–120. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-019-01406-y.
Fang, Shaoying, Naoki Marumo, and Akiko Takeda. 2026. Parameter-Free Cubic-Regularized Newton Method: Sharp Complexity and Generalized Smoothness. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2607.10741.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Floor.Semiring
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.PointwiseHessianStationarity

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L₀ : ℝ
  L₁ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
abbrev Reply (p : Params) := ℝ × Point p × (Point p →L[ℝ] Point p)

abbrev broadSpec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Point p → ℝ
  Query := Point
  Reply := Reply
  Output := Point
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.L₀ ∧ 0 ≤ p.L₁ ∧ 0 < p.L₀ + p.L₁ ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.G ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 3 f ∧
    (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) x‖ ≤ p.L₀ + p.L₁ * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    (∀ x, f 0 - f x ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ‖gradient f 0‖ ≤ p.G ∧
    (∀ history seed x, O.answer history (0, x) seed =
      (f x, gradient f x, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x))
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

abbrev spec : Setup := { broadSpec with
  valid := fun p => broadSpec.valid p ∧ 16 * p.ε ≤ p.G ∧
    2 ^ 39 ≤ p.Δ * Real.sqrt (p.L₀ + p.L₁ * p.ε) / (p.ε * Real.sqrt p.ε) ∧
    2 ^ 140 * (1 + ⌈p.Δ * Real.sqrt (p.L₀ + p.L₁ * p.ε) / (p.ε * Real.sqrt p.ε)⌉₊) ^ 4 ≤ p.d }

end LongTails.Setups.PointwiseHessianStationarity
